title: Whole Concentric Porous Tests and Polar Spines Radiolarian
description: One wholly newly authored enlarged radiolarian-inspired empty skeletal teaching prop. Two complete concentric thick-walled spherical tests each have eighty genuine polygonal through-pores and a hollow interior. Six continuous radial beams connect the full shells at shared lattice junctions; two opposing beams extend uninterrupted into tapered polar spines. All shell tessellation, pore rims, radial connections and numeric coordinates are new. No elongated diatom valve, raphe, girdle, cell shell, decorative wire ball, fruit or old animal geometry is copied, extracted or recoloured. Eight closed editable components, three opaque warm mineral PBR roles, one complete skeleton prop and zero scenes, roughly seventeen centimetres long at an arbitrary enlarged display scale. The small lower exterior lattice datum is flattened for display only. This is a deliberately regularized generic morphology, not a named species or measured specimen: shell number, pore pattern, beam and spine counts are schematic rather than taxonomic characters. Soft cytoplasm, central capsule, nucleus and axopodia are intentionally not represented in this empty-test asset. No claim of living function, growth, optical silica, fossil age, buoyancy, filtering, mechanics, physical stability or scientific simulation. No labels, textures, transparency, rig, animation or interaction.
